extracted.intended_audience: PARI/GP users and script authors (mathematicians/number-theorists/programmers) wanting to produce plots and write gp programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and reference for using PARI/GP plotting functions (high- and low-level, PostScript output, virtual rectwindows) and for GP control statements and debugging primitives. Includes function semantics, flags, caveats and examples for writing scripts and interactive gp sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three types of graphic functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification: (1) High-level plotting functions (ploth*), (2) Low-level plotting functions (plot* rectwindow API), (3) Functions for PostScript output (ps*).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use high-level for simple plots, low-level for manual drawing primitives and composition via rectwindows, and ps* functions to produce PostScript output appended to psfile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initialize rectwindows before use
rubrics_metrics.description: There are 16 virtual windows (rectwindows) numbered 0..15 that must be initialized before being used by plotinit, which specifies height and width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: plotinit sets the virtual cursor to [0,0]. Use plotcursor to obtain the current cursor. Failing to call plotinit before using low-level functions is incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual cursor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rectwindow has an associated virtual cursor initialized at [0,0]; some plotting primitives are relative to this cursor (plotr*), others use absolute coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plotmove/plotrmove to set/move cursor; plotr* variants draw relative to current cursor. Many routines do or do not move the cursor—read each function's note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rect objects clipping behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Rect objects drawn in a rectwindow use the window's default color and only the part inside the window is drawn, except polygons and strings which are drawn entirely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware polygons and strings are not clipped; use plotclip if you need to remove invisible parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Window preservation and erasure policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Rectwindows are preserved so further drawings using same windows at different positions or different windows can be done without extra work. It is not possible to partially erase a window: you must erase it completely with plotkill and reinitialize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To remove previous content, call plotkill then plotinit; avoid expecting partial erasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use plotscale to avoid conversions / set coordinate system
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless plotscale is called, scaling is the number of pixels with origin at upper-left and y-coordinates going downwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call plotscale to set a convenient coordinate system (e.g., [0,1000]×[0,1000]) to avoid manual pixel conversions and to orient axes as desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plotting platform independence and drivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Plotting functions are platform independent; graphical drivers exist for X11-windows, Qt and FLTK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen output depends on available driver; some features (colors, etc.) only implemented for certain drivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotdraw forks and leaves gp usable
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical window opened by plotdraw or ploth* is completely separated from gp (fork is done, non-graphical memory freed in child), so you can continue working in current gp session while the window is open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Window manager controls (close/enlarge/reduce) work as usual; no zooming implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: PostScript output appended to psfile
rubrics_metrics.description: ps* functions (psdraw, psploth, psplothraw) write PostScript output appended to the psfile default (./pari.ps unless changed). Each new PS output is appended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove or change psfile between plots if you do not want them concatenated into a single file; you can use PS output even without plotting routines enabled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics not available in PARI library mode
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the graphic functions are available within the PARI library; you must be under gp to use them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you insist on using these in compiled programs, inspect plot*.c sources, but prefer specialized graphical tools for heavy-duty graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: plot(X = a, b, expr, {Ymin},{Ymax}) ASCII plotting
rubrics_metrics.description: Crude ASCII plot of expr from a to b with Y ranging from Ymin to Ymax. If Ymin/Ymax omitted, computed min/max of expr values are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for quick ASCII visual checks; not for publication-quality plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotbox(w,x2,y2): rectangle outline from cursor to corner
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw the outline of the rectangle whose opposite corners are (x1,y1) current cursor and (x2,y2) in rectwindow w. Only part inside w is drawn; cursor does not move.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plotrbox for relative offsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotclip(w): clip content to visible area
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes all parts of the drawing that would not be visible on the screen in rectwindow w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use together with plotcopy to draw on a scratchpad before committing visible portions to final picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotcolor(w,c): set default color per rectwindow
rubrics_metrics.description: Set default color c in rectwindow w. Implemented only for X-windows, fltk and Qt. Default mapping given by graphcolormap (1=black,2=blue,...), and can be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check your driver for supported colors and extend graphcolormap if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotcopy(sourcew,destw,dx,dy,{flag=0}): copy window contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Copy contents of rectwindow sourcew to destw with offset (dx,dy). If flag's bit 1 set, dx/dy are fractions of device size; otherwise pixels. Other flag bits change anchoring corner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use flag bits to interpret offsets as fractions and to choose NW/SW/SE/NE anchoring as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotcursor(w): get current scaled cursor position
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the current (scaled) position of the virtual cursor corresponding to rectwindow w as a 2-component vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to programmatically query current drawing position.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotdraw(list,{flag=0}): physically place and draw rectwindows
rubrics_metrics.description: Given list = [w1,x1,y1,w2,x2,y2,...], physically place windows w1,w2,... with their upper-left corner at given physical positions and draw them; overlapping regions are drawn twice and windows are transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=0, xi,yi express fractions of device size; list length must be divisible by 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: ploth(X=a,b,expr,{flags=0},{n=0}): high-precision plotting
rubrics_metrics.description: High precision plot of y=f(x) from a to b. Opens a window (killed on click) and returns [xmin,xmax,ymin,ymax]. ploth may evaluate expr thousands of times; n sets number of reference points (0 uses defaults).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important note: ploth may evaluate expr thousands of times; keep current precision low (e.g. 9) before calling. If expr is vector, multiple curves drawn. Try varying parameters if recursive plotting yields polygonal artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ploth flags: meaning of binary bits
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitflags control plot mode and display options. Key bits: 1=Parametric, 2=Recursive, 4=no Rescale, 8=no X axis, 16=no Y axis, 32=no Frame, 64=no Lines, 128=Points too, 256=Splines, 512=no X ticks, 1024=no Y ticks, 2048=Same ticks, 4096=Complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine bits to produce desired effects (e.g., Parametric|no_Rescale). Examples provided (parametric circles, recursive pitfalls).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recursive plotting caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursive plotting (flag 2) adaptively inserts midpoints unless midpoints are close to segments. It is fast and often more precise but can produce polygonal approximations that poorly represent the curve if unlucky or if too few reference points chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never plot recursively an odd function on a symmetric interval around 0; try plotting with slightly different parameters to check for artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: plothraw(listx,listy,{flag=0}): high-precision point plotting
rubrics_metrics.description: Plots points given by listx and listy vectors. Automatic positioning and scaling done; if flag=1, join points; other flags combine as in ploth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when plotting raw point datasets; use flag=1 to connect points.

rubrics_metrics.name: plothsizes({flag=0}): query output device sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a 6-component vector: window width, height, tick sizes (horizontal and vertical), width and height of characters. If flag=0 values are pixels; otherwise fractions of screen size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to portably initialize windows with maximum size.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotinit(w,{x},{y},{flag=0}): initialize rectwindow
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize rectwindow w, destroying any rect objects drawn in w. Virtual cursor set to (0,0). x,y set width/height; omitting uses full device size. If flag=0, x,y are in pixels; otherwise fractions of device size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Device-imposed upper bounds available via plothsizes. To create device-independent coords use plothsizes + plotinit + plotscale (example provided to set [0,1000]×[0,1000]).

rubrics_metrics.name: plotkill(w): erase and free rectwindow
rubrics_metrics.description: Erase rectwindow w and free corresponding memory. To reuse w you must call plotinit to specify new size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer plotinit when you want to discard previous work as it reinitializes window.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotlines(w,X,Y,{flag=0}): draw polygon/segments
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw polygon whose vertices are in vectors X and Y (draw whole polygon, not only part inside rectwindow). If flag non-zero, close polygon. If X and Y are scalars, draw just the single segment from cursor to (X,Y) and move cursor to (X,Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If starting point isn't current cursor, use plotmove before calling plotlines to set start explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotlinetype(w,type): change line type
rubrics_metrics.description: Change type of subsequently plotted lines in rectwindow w. type = -2 corresponds to frames, -1 to axes; larger values may mean other styles. w = -1 changes high-level plotting. Only used by gnuplot interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functionality depends on gnuplot interface; check mapping of type codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotmove(w,x,y): reposition virtual cursor
rubrics_metrics.description: Move the virtual cursor of rectwindow w to position (x,y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to set explicit starting points for relative drawing commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotpoints(w,X,Y): draw points
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw points whose coordinates are in vectors X and Y and that lie inside w. The virtual cursor does not move. If X and Y are scalars, draw the single point and move the virtual cursor to that position (even if outside window).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to plothraw but with no scaling or with plotscale-chosen scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotpointsize(w,size): set successive point sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Change the size of following points in rectwindow w. If w = -1 change globally. Only works in gnuplot interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Size changes affect later point plotting calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotpointtype(w,type): set point marker type
rubrics_metrics.description: Change the type of points subsequently plotted in rectwindow w. type = -1 corresponds to a dot; w = -1 changes high-level plotting. Only taken into account by gnuplot interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check gnuplot mapping of type integers to marker shapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrbox(w,dx,dy): draw relative rectangle outline
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw rectangle outline in rectwindow w where opposite corners are (x1,y1) current cursor and (x1+dx,y1+dy). Only part inside w is drawn; virtual cursor does not move.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when building shapes relative to current cursor position.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrecth(w,X=a,b,expr,{flag=0},{n=0}): write ploth output to rectwindow
rubrics_metrics.description: Writes to rectwindow w the curve output of ploth with given parameters and returns a vector for the bounding box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to compose high-precision plots into rectwindows for later combination via plotdraw.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrecthraw(w,data,{flags=0}): plot data into rectwindow
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot graph(s) for data in rectwindow w. data is vector of vectors: if parametric, must be even number of vectors; otherwise first vector is x coordinates and other vectors are y-coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recursive plotting flag not significant here; use flags as in ploth for display options.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrline(w,dx,dy): draw relative segment and move cursor
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw part of segment (x1,y1)-(x1+dx,y1+dy) inside w, where (x1,y1) is current cursor, and move virtual cursor to (x1+dx,y1+dy) even if outside window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for incremental line drawing.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrmove(w,dx,dy): move cursor relative to initial cursor
rubrics_metrics.description: Move virtual cursor of rectwindow w to position (x1+dx,y1+dy) relative to initial cursor position (x1,y1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when implementing relative positioning sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotrpoint(w,dx,dy): draw relative point and move cursor
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw point (x1+dx,y1+dy) on rectwindow w if inside w and move virtual cursor to that position; (x1,y1) is current cursor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines point drawing and advancing cursor for subsequent relative drawing.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotscale(w,x1,x2,y1,y2): set coordinate scaling for a rectwindow
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale local coordinates of rectwindow w so x goes from x1 to x2 and y from y1 to y2. Initially default is pixel coordinates with y downward; plotscale overrides defaults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always use plotscale when graphing to get predictable axes, especially when combining multiple functions on a rectwindow.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotstring(w,x,{flags=0}): draw text at cursor with justification flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw the string x at the current cursor in rectwindow w. Flag bits 1 and 2 control horizontal alignment (left=0,right=2,center=1). Bits 4 and 8 control vertical alignment (bottom=0,top=8,v-center=4). Bits 16/32 insert small horizontal/vertical gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See tutorial for usage examples; flags allow precise text placement relative to cursor.

rubrics_metrics.name: psdraw(list,{flag=0}): PostScript drawing of rectwindows
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as plotdraw, but output is a PostScript program appended to the psfile. flag!=0 scales the plot from current device size to standard PostScript plotting size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine with psploth/psplothraw to generate PS files for printing or archiving.

rubrics_metrics.name: psploth/psplothraw: produce PostScript plots
rubrics_metrics.description: psploth and psplothraw are the PostScript equivalents of ploth and plothraw, generating PS programs appended to psfile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for generating publication-quality PostScript output; remember psfile is appended to each time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexical scoping of loop variables in gp
rubrics_metrics.description: In constructs like for(X=a,b,seq) the variable X is lexically scoped to the loop and may shadow an outer variable; modifying the loop index inside seq changes the loop behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with variable reuse: e.g., assigning to the outer variable name inside the loop won't restore outer binding; example given where n is restored after loop only if not mutated inside the loop body.

rubrics_metrics.name: break({n=1}): exit enclosing loops
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrupts execution of current seq and immediately exits from the n innermost enclosing loops within current function call (or top-level). n must be positive; if greater than number of loops, all loops are exited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to break out of nested loops; be explicit with n when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: breakpoint(): enter break loop for interactive debugging
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrupts the program and enter the breakloop. Program continues when breakloop exited. In breakloop you can inspect variables and resume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for interactive debugging; example demonstrates invoking and inspecting local variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: dbg_down({n=1}) and dbg_up({n=1}) frame navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the break loop dbg_down goes down n frames, canceling previous dbg_up; dbg_up goes up n frames to inspect parent function frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to navigate the call stack in the breakloop while debugging.

rubrics_metrics.name: dbg_err(): retrieve current error data in break loop
rubrics_metrics.description: In the break loop, dbg_err() returns the error data of the current error; use Vec(dbg_err()) or similar to inspect components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for diagnosing exceptions; see iferr for catching errors programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: dbg_x(A,{n}): print internal structure for debugging
rubrics_metrics.description: Print the inner structure of A up to level n (complete if n omitted). Similar to \x but does not require A to be a history entry; works in break loop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handy for inspecting complex GEN objects while debugging.

rubrics_metrics.name: for(X=a,b,seq): basic numeric for-loop
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq where X goes from a to b. Nothing is done if a>b. a and b must be in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard iteration; be mindful of lexical scoping of X.

rubrics_metrics.name: forcomposite(n=a,{b},seq): iterate composite numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq where n ranges over composite numbers between a and b inclusive. Omitting b runs through all composites >= a (infinite loop expected to be broken by user). n may not be modified inside seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for composite-specific routines; watch out for infinite loops when b omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: fordiv(n,X,seq): iterate divisors of n
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq with X ranging through divisors of n. n can be an integer or a factorization matrix; divisors are sorted by increasing size if n is integer. A constant-space slower alternative FORDIV is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fordiv for speed and convenience; for huge divisor sets consider memory and use streaming approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: forell(E,a,b,seq): iterate elliptic curves by conductor
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq where E = [name,M,G] ranges through elliptic curves of conductors from a to b. Requires elldata database installed with relevant data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for batch processing Cremona curve data; library syntax provided for low-level calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: forpart(X=k,seq,{a=k},{n=k}): iterate integer partitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate seq over partitions X = [x1,...,xn] of integer k. Optional n restricts number of parts; a restricts maximum part sizes; default behavior removes zeros unless amin ≤ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior unspecified if X is modified inside loop; use parameters to constrain lengths and parts (examples given).

rubrics_metrics.name: forprime(p=a,{b},seq): iterate primes
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq where p ranges over primes between a and b, incrementing to nextprime(p+1). Omitting b loops over all primes ≥ a (infinite loop expected to be broken by user). p may not be modified inside seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenient for prime-based algorithms; avoid modifying the loop variable inside body.

rubrics_metrics.name: forstep(X=a,b,s,seq): iterate with custom steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq where X goes from a to b in increments of s. s can be scalar or a vector of steps; nothing is done if s>0 and a>b or s<0 and a<b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vector steps to cycle through a pattern of increments (example provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: forsubgroup(H=G,{bound},seq): iterate subgroups of abelian group
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq for each subgroup H of abelian group G (SNF form or elementary divisors). If bound present restrict to index < bound or exact index. Subgroups not ordered except p-groups; subgroup given as generator matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when enumerating subgroups; to canonicalize output, convert with mathnf(concat(G,H)).

rubrics_metrics.name: forvec(X=v,seq,{flag=0}): lexicographic vector iteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Let v be n-component vector of [ai,bi] pairs. Routine iterates X lexicographically from [a1,...,an] to [b1,...,bn]. flag=1 generates only nondecreasing X, flag=2 only strictly increasing X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for nested multi-index loops without explicit nesting; note ordering of indices (highest index moves fastest).

rubrics_metrics.name: if(a,{seq1},{seq2}): conditional expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate seq1 if a is non-zero, otherwise seq2. The if returns the value of evaluated branch. Supports chained tests to implement switch/case style constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boolean operators && and || short-circuit; remember if is not a loop so loop-only constructs like break/next don't apply to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: iferr(seq1,E,seq2{,pred}): error-catching and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq1; if an error occurs set E to error data and, if pred absent or true, evaluate seq2 (which can reference E). The value of iferr is seq2 if error occurs, seq1 otherwise. seq2 should check errname(E) and component(E,...) to validate error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can rethrow error using error(E). Comprehensive list of error types and the structure/components of E is provided and should be used to write robust error handlers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed error taxonomy for iferr
rubrics_metrics.description: List of valid error types (e.g., "e_ARCH","e_BUG","e_FILE","e_MEM","e_INV","e_PRIME", etc.) with the meaning of each and the components of error data E (what component(E,i) contains).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use errname(E) and component(E,i) to inspect and discriminate errors programmatically in iferr handlers; the manual lists all categories and expected components.

rubrics_metrics.name: next({n=1}): resume next iteration of enclosing loop
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrupt execution of current seq and resume at the next iteration of the n-th enclosing loop (default 1). If n exceeds number of loops, all loops are exited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to continue to next iteration in nested loops; supply n to target outer loops.

rubrics_metrics.name: return({x=0}): return from subroutine
rubrics_metrics.description: Return from current subroutine with result x. If omitted, returns a void-like (no result) value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to exit functions early with a value.

rubrics_metrics.name: until(a,seq) and while(a,seq): loop variants
rubrics_metrics.description: until(a,seq) evaluates seq and then tests a (execute until a is non-zero); while(a,seq) tests a before running seq (execute while a non-zero).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose until for do-while semantics and while for precondition looping; be careful with initial conditions (until runs body once if a initially non-zero).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strprintf(fmt,{x}*): formatted string construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a string built from arguments according to format fmt (like printf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for building messages and dynamic help strings; format specifiers follow printf conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: addhelp(sym,str): attach help text to symbol
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes the help message for symbol sym. The string str is expanded on the spot and stored as online help for the symbol. Recommended to document globals and user functions this way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aliases will not show addhelp text (alias help forwards to target symbol). After addhelp the function code is omitted from the help display but remains accessible by typing the function name.

rubrics_metrics.name: alarm({s=0},{code}): schedule or cancel timeout
rubrics_metrics.description: If code omitted, trigger an e_ALARM exception after s seconds, canceling previously set alarm; stop a pending alarm if s=0 or omitted. An optional code may be associated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to implement timeouts in scripts; handle e_ALARM in iferr handlers if needed.
